{{nihongo|'''Kushida Shrine (Matsusaka)'''|櫛田神社 (松阪市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ise Province]].

'''Kushida Shrine''' (くしだじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Kushida-chō, {{ill|Matsusaka|Q460829|qid=Q460829}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}} its former rank was {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

It is located near the west bank of the lower {{ill|Kushida River|Q6447936|qid=Q6447936}}. It is revered by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=barber}} and {{ill|Cosmetology|Q2474068|qid=Q2474068}} professionals, and near the precinct stands a “{{ill|Comb|Q23834|qid=Q23834}} monument” built by the Mie Prefectural Beauty and Sanitation Trade Association and others. {{ill|Kushida Shrine|Q865839|qid=Q865839|lt=Kushida Shrine}} in Hakata Ward, Fukuoka City, known for July’s {{ill|Hakata Gion Yamakasa|Q1749262|qid=Q1749262}} and October’s {{ill|Hakata Okunchi|Q11408922|qid=Q11408922}}, is said to have been founded in {{ill|AD 757|Q31135|qid=Q31135}} ({{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|de|Tempyō-Hōji|es|Tenpyō-hōji|fa|تنپیو-هوجی|fr|Ère Tenpyō-hōji|ia|Tenpyo-hoji|id|Tempyō-hōji|ja|天平宝字|ko|덴표호지|ru|Тэмпё-ходзи|simple|Tenpyō-hōji|sr|Тенпјо хоџи|tr|Tenpyō-hōji|uk|Темпьо-Ходзі (ненґо)|zh|天平宝字|zh_yue|天平寶字|qid=Q1346307}} 1) by inviting this shrine.

=== Enshrined deities ===
Its {{ill|Saijin|abstract|Q11591100|fr|Saijin|ja|祭神|zh|祭神|qid=Q11591100}} are {{ill|Ōwakako no Mikoto|Q111114032|qid=Q111114032}}, Kushitamahime-no-Mikoto, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|abstract|Q272993|ar|سوسانو|azb|سوسانو|bcl|Susanoo|be|Сусанаа|bg|Сусаноо|ca|Susanoo|cs|Susanoo|da|Susa-no-o|de|Susanoo|el|Σουσάνoο|eo|Susanoo|es|Susanoo|eu|Susanoo|fa|سوسانو (خدا)|fi|Susanoo|fr|Susanoo|hr|Susano|hu|Szuszanoo|hy|Սուսանո|id|Susanoo|it|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ|ka|სუსანოო-ნო-მიკოტო|ko|스사노오|la|Susano'o|lb|Susanoo|mni|ꯁꯨꯁꯅꯨ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|nl|Susanoo|pl|Susanoo|pt|Susanoo|ro|Susanoo|rsk|Сусано|ru|Сусаноо|simple|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|sl|Susanovo|sr|Сусаноо|su|Susanoo|sv|Susanoo|ta|சுசானவோ|th|ซูซาโนโอะ|tok|jan sewi Susano|tr|Susanoo|uk|Сусаноо|vi|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|zh|素戔嗚尊|zh_min_nan|Susanoo|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Oshihomimi}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ichikishima-hime}}.

Ōwakago-no-Mikoto, according to ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|Q131331326|qid=Q131331326}}'', was a powerful local ruler governing “Takeda no Kuni”; after {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|es|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|fa|یاماتوهیمه نو میکوتو|fr|Yamatohime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|mni|ꯌꯃꯇꯣꯍꯤꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|vi|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|zh|倭姬命|qid=Q4388732}} interacted with him while visiting this area, a comb fell, so the place was named Kushida and “Kushida-sha” was established<ref>[https://www.matsusaka-kanko.com/information/2017/01/06/櫛田神社/] - “Kushida Shrine,” Matsusaka Tourism Association</ref><ref> ''{{ill|Yamatohime no Mikoto Seiki|Q131331326|qid=Q131331326}}''</ref>.

Also, according to the shrine history, because Ōwakago-no-Mikoto achieved many military merits, Yamatohime-no-Mikoto ordered that he be enshrined as this shrine’s deity.

=== History ===
Shrine tradition says it was founded in year 22 of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}} ({{ill|Ante Christum natum|Q28200|qid=Q28200}}), when {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|es|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|fa|یاماتوهیمه نو میکوتو|fr|Yamatohime no Mikoto|ja|倭姫命|mni|ꯌꯃꯇꯣꯍꯤꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|vi|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|zh|倭姬命|qid=Q4388732}} was searching for a place to enshrine {{ill|Amaterasu|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qid=Q455602}} and enshrined Ōwakago-no-Mikoto, who guided her here. Around the {{ill|Meireki|Q1192766|qid=Q1192766}} period in the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, shrine buildings were lost and worship lapsed, but it was revived in the {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} era.

On {{ill|February 27|Q2361|qid=Q2361}}, {{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 40), it was relocated to Aza Murogaito and renamed Ōkushida Shrine with {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|Q11412524|qid=Q11412524}}; on {{ill|February 11|Q2335|qid=Q2335}}, {{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}} (Meiji 41), it was merged into {{ill|Iinotakamiya-kouyama Shrine|Q17988632|qid=Q17988632}} in Yamazoe-chō. Later, {{ill|Ujiko|Q125562175|qid=Q125562175}} requested a {{ill|Bunrei|Q195793|qid=Q195793}}, and on {{ill|February 1|Q2312|qid=Q2312}}, {{ill|1933|Q18726|qid=Q18726}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 8), a divided shrine was re-established at the current site.

On {{ill|September 4|Q2855|qid=Q2855}}, {{ill|2006|Q2021|qid=Q2021}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 18) (Comb Day), a “{{ill|Comb|Q23834|qid=Q23834}} monument” was erected by the Mie Prefectural Beauty and Sanitation Trade Association and others. The calligraphy was by then {{ill|Minister of Health, Labour and Welfare|Q841962|qid=Q841962}} {{ill|Jirō Kawasaki|Q1689655|qid=Q1689655}}.
